topicName: Version Control, Git Integration, and Forking
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Version Control, Git Integration, and Forking in Postman"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Effective API development requires robust collaboration, tracking changes, and managing multiple versions of collections. Postman provides native Git integration and forking capabilities to streamline collaborative API workflows."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Postman Forking"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A fork is essentially an independent copy of a collection. It allows developers to make modifications, add requests, or alter test scripts without impacting the original parent collection. Once changes are tested and verified, you can merge them back."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Navigate to the desired collection in your workspace sidebar."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click on the three-dot menu (...) next to the collection name and select 'Create a fork'."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Select your target workspace and provide a label for your fork."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Pull Requests and Merging Changes"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"After working on your forked collection, you can propose your changes to the parent collection by creating a pull request. This initiates a review process similar to traditional Git workflows."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Open your forked collection and click 'Create Pull Request'."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Add a descriptive title and summary detailing your updates."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Assign reviewers to evaluate your changes before merging them into the parent collection."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Git Repository Integration"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Postman allows you to connect your collections directly to external Git repositories like GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps. This ensures your API definitions and test scripts remain in sync with your source code repository."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Open the collection settings and select the 'Git' tab."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Authorize Postman to access your Git provider and select the target repository and branch."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure the directory path where your collection JSON files will be stored."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Example: Automating Git Sync via Postman CLI"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can also run and sync your collections using the Postman CLI (Postman CLI) within your CI/CD pipelines to validate API tests against your Git branches."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"postman login --with-api-key <YOUR_POSTMAN_API_KEY>\npostman collection run <COLLECTION_ID> --environment <ENVIRONMENT_ID>"}]
